# Town library translation pilot
The library calls its bilingual reading cards "a visible expression of our commitment to language access". This is the institution's stated meaning of the cards, not a measured user response. The pilot supplied 24 printed cards in Spanish and Arabic at two branches for four weeks.
Staff received 18 unsolicited comments, 13 favorable and 5 reporting unclear wording. Visitors were not sampled systematically; the number who used the cards is unknown. Three Arabic cards were revised after staff found incorrect opening hours. The Spanish cards had correct opening hours, although two Spanish readers reported wording difficulty. One Arabic reader praised the welcoming design while reporting a wrong closing time.
No comprehension or belonging survey was conducted. A website version is proposed, with no release date or completed implementation. The annual circulation total predates the pilot and cannot measure its effect.

Idea.Title: Stated access commitment and the limits of the card pilot
Idea.Description: Explain the library's explicit meaning, the actual pilot and feedback limits, separating wording and factual accuracy from measured inclusion.
Idea.Rationale: Separate supported observations from stronger conclusions and preserve the relevant contrast.
Idea.Evidence: Cards express the library's commitment; positive comments establish that comprehension and belonging improved.
